closureVerdicts.item: RENDER-2 — historyValid uniform gates the EMA seed; Swift↔Metal layout in sync
closureVerdicts.trace: Layout parity verified field-by-field, not asserted: both structs carry 28 members in identical order and identical widths; `historyValid` lands at byte offset 136 on BOTH sides (SemanticMatte.metal:40-43 and SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:138-141), struct size 156 → stride 160, which is exactly what `setBytes(length: MemoryLayout<MatteUniforms>.stride)` (SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:412) ships. simd_float3x3/float3x3 agree at 48 bytes/align 16, Int32/int and UInt32/uint at 4. Write-timing traced and SOUND: `matteHistoryValid=false` on every (re)alloc (SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:511,523) and on uninstall (:216); set true only after the dispatch is encoded (:435). Ping-pong: previous=matteTextures[matteIndex], next=matteTextures[1-matteIndex], then matteIndex flips to the slot just WRITTEN (:344-346) — so the next encode's `previousMatte` is precisely the texture the previous dispatch wrote, never the never-written twin. The first frame after a realloc reads nothing (historyValid=0, kernel seeds `previous = matte`, SemanticMatte.metal:243-244) and writes slot 1; frame 2 reads slot 1; frame 3 reads slot 0 written by frame 2. Same-queue command buffers commit in order, so 'true after CPU encode' is sound. Bail frames do not flip matteIndex (all three bails precede :346), so a stale-but-written slot is the worst case. Kernel writes nextMatte unconditionally for every in-bounds gid (:247), so 'written' means fully written. NOTE (gap, not a defect): no test asserts the layout — the struct is `private`, so a future one-sided field insertion would silently corrupt every uniform past the divergence (refineRadius garbage → an unbounded guided-filter loop). Worth a stride/offset guard in a later wave.

closureVerdicts.item: RENDER-1 step 1 — pass detach dwell floor (15 s idle AND 10 s since attach)
closureVerdicts.trace: Built at GeoARSessionManager.swift:1219-1232 with `passAttachedAt` at :1235. Anti-thrash goal is met (minimum toggle period ≥15 s). But the second conjunct at :1227 is provably unreachable: `passIdleSince` is assigned ONLY in the `!passNeeded` branch (:1231) and cleared in the `passNeeded` branch (:1220) immediately before `passAttachedAt` is stamped (:1222), so passAttachedAt ≤ passIdleSince invariantly ⇒ now−passAttachedAt ≥ now−passIdleSince > 15 > 10 whenever the first conjunct passes. closureVerdicts.item: RENDER-3 — releaseCaptureResources() on detach + uninstall
closureVerdicts.trace: SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:188-193 (detach edge, inside stateLock) and :218 (uninstall), helper at :453-458. Correctly serialized with the render thread: encode holds stateLock for its whole body (:267-268), so the main-actor CVMetalTextureCacheFlush can never race a CVMetalTextureCacheCreateTextureFromImage. In the steady state inFlightTextures is already empty at detach (success path moves it to `retained` at :423-424, bail paths removeAll at :442), so the flush is the load-bearing half; wrappers from the last encoded frame self-release on GPU completion (:425-427). Lock-order invariant documented (:66-69) and honoured: encode takes stateLock then feed locks (:289, :314); disarmSemanticMatte takes the feed lock and releases it BEFORE taking stateLock (GeoARSessionManager.swift:410 then :411) — never nested in reverse.

closureVerdicts.item: RENDER-4 — prepare(device:) builds Metal state outside the lock, commits with a lost-race discard
closureVerdicts.trace: SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:222-253. Probe under lock (:228-231), library load + pipeline compile + cache create + 3 dummies outside (:233-242), commit under lock with `if pipeline != nil, self.device === device { return }` (:246). Race-discard is correct: the loser's locals are simply released, and the commit block writes device/pipeline/textureCache/dummies atomically w.r.t. encode, so no torn set can be observed. The `pipeline == nil, device === device` case (post-uninstall) correctly rebuilds rather than short-circuiting. Doc comment + lock-order invariant corrected at :62-69 and :79-82.

closureVerdicts.item: RENDER-5 — MidFieldDepthEstimator copies on the QUEUE via SourceBox into pooled buffers; box empties pre-inference
closureVerdicts.trace: MidFieldDepthEstimator.swift:152 (box built on the main actor from frame.capturedImage + sceneDepth.depthMap), :161-163 (both pooledCopy calls, then `sources.empty()` BEFORE the VNImageRequestHandler at :173) — the ARKit buffers are released pre-inference as claimed. Release semantics verified: the closure captures only `sources`, `timestamp`, `model`, `self` — NOT `frame` and not `lidarSource`, so nothing else retains the originals; the only early exit above empty() is `guard let self` (:155), which destroys the closure context and hence the box anyway. `busy` (:137, reset in the defer at :156-160) bounds the app to ONE in-flight box, and `loadIfNeeded` shares the same serial queue but sets `model` only at the end (:122), so no box is ever created while the 50 MB decode occupies the queue. Pool reuse at 5 Hz is sound: pooled buffers are locals released at closure end and are never published (the published Sample carries Vision's own output buffer, :181-189), so CVPixelBufferPoolCreatePixelBuffer always recycles. `copyContents` stride-mismatch branch (:284-291) copies min(srcStride,dstStride) ≥ visible row bytes for both planes — padding garbage from a recycled pool buffer is never read back (Vision and fitInverseDepth both index by width within stride). vImage downscaler correctly deferred.

findings.title: RENDER-1's dwell floor is a dead conjunct plus a tripled idle-attached window: the 10 s min-attach term can never bind, so the pass now burns ADR-035's offscreen-render cost for 15 s of no work instead of 5 s
findings.trace: The detach rule is `Date().timeIntervalSince(since) > 15, Date().timeIntervalSince(passAttachedAt) > 10` (:1226-1227). `passIdleSince` is assigned ONLY at :1231, in the `!passNeeded` branch; the `passNeeded` branch clears it at :1220 and only then stamps `passAttachedAt` at :1222. Therefore passAttachedAt <= passIdleSince holds invariantly on every path (setCallbacksActive(true) has no other call site — grep confirms :1224 is the only one), which gives now-passAttachedAt >= now-passIdleSince > 15 > 10 whenever the first conjunct passes. The second conjunct is unreachable and the effective rule is `idle > 15` alone, i.e. round 2 changed 5 s to 15 s (diff line: `- if Date().timeIntervalSince(since) > 5 {`) and paid for it with a term that contributes nothing. During those extra 10 s the callbacks are still installed, so RealityKit forces the offscreen render + full-screen copy path every frame and SemanticOcclusionPass.encode falls through the `guard semanticEnabled || personEnabled || midEnabled` at SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:330 into bailOut → blit (:493-497) on every single frame.
findings.harm: Every idle episode (person walks out of frame, content leaves view, thermal sheds the depth streams) now costs ~15 s x 60 fps ≈ 900 forced offscreen renders + full-screen source→target blits instead of ~300 — roughly 600 extra full-screen copies per episode, repeated on each cycle across a 10-minute session. That is precisely the regression ADR-035 exists to prevent, charged against the charter's 'not thermal .serious at 10 min' and ≥30 fps bars, and it buys nothing: the anti-thrash guarantee round 2 wanted (bounded toggle period on the one cross-thread mutation RealityKit does not synchronize) is delivered entirely by the min-attach term, which as written can never fire.
findings.fix: Put the guarantee in the conjunct that can bind and give the idle window back: restore the idle threshold to 5 s and let the 10 s min-attach floor set the toggle period — `if Date().timeIntervalSince(since) > 5, Date().timeIntervalSince(passAttachedAt) > 10`. Toggle period stays ≥10 s (attach at T, work ends at T+1, idle satisfied T+6, detach held to T+10) while idle-attached time drops from 15 s to ≤9 s and to 5 s whenever work ran longer than 10 s. Extract the decision as `nonisolated static func shouldDetachPass(now:idleSince:attachedAt:) -> Bool` so both conjuncts are table-testable, and reset `passIdleSince = nil` on the detach so the state is not left dangling.

findings.title: RENDER-6's 'measured, not asserted' buffer hold starts the clock after the queue wait, so it under-reports exactly under the thermal pressure it exists to detect
findings.trace: `update(pixelBuffer:)` retains the ARKit capture-pool buffer the instant the closure is formed at `queue.async` (:45) — that is when the hold begins. `let holdStart = Date()` is sampled INSIDE the closure at :47, i.e. after the block has already been dequeued and started running. The measured interval at :52 therefore covers only `handler.perform` (:79) and excludes the queue-wait component. The comment at :49-51 claims the hold is measured and that a hold past 100 ms 'means the pool is under real pressure' — but the pressure scenario the counsel raised is precisely the system deprioritising the queue, which manifests as dequeue latency, not as a longer perform().
findings.harm: On a device where the fps sawtooth is being caused by capture-pool starvation from a delayed sentinel block, the field trace shows no 'PersonSentinel buffer hold exceeded 100 ms' line at all, because perform() on a downscaled human-rectangle pass is a few ms regardless. The one instrument round 2 added to attribute the sawtooth correctly reports clean under the failure it was built for, sending the frame-budget investigation toward thermal throttling (which the charter explicitly warns 'reads as thermal throttling but isn't').
findings.fix: Sample the start on the caller's side, where the retain actually happens, and capture it: `let holdStart = Date()` immediately before `queue.async`, then `queue.async { [weak self, holdStart] in ... }`. Also store the last measured hold (e.g. `private(set) var lastHoldSeconds`) or accept an injectable clock so the measurement itself is testable rather than log-only.

testCases.name: testPassDetachRequiresIdleAndMinAttachIndependently
testCases.asserts: Against an extracted pure `GeoARSessionManager.shouldDetachPass(now:idleSince:attachedAt:)`, a three-row table: (a) idleSince = now-6, attachedAt = now-12 → TRUE (6 s idle, 12 s attached clears the 10 s min-attach floor, so the pass must detach); (b) idleSince = now-6, attachedAt = now-8 → FALSE (min-attach floor not met — the anti-thrash conjunct binds); (c) idleSince = now-2, attachedAt = now-600 → FALSE (idle window not met). Plus an invariant row asserting attachedAt <= idleSince is the only reachable ordering, documenting why the current 15/10 pair collapses to one term.
testCases.failsWhen: Row (a) fails on the round-2 build: the live rule requires idle > 15 s, so it returns FALSE at 6 s idle and the pass stays attached for another 9 s of forced offscreen render + blit. Vacuity-proofed in both directions — rows (b) and (c) are FALSE, so a stub that always returns true fails; row (a) is TRUE, so a stub that always returns false (and the current 15 s-only rule) fails. Row (b) is the specific guard against 'fixing' this by simply lowering 15 to 5 and deleting the min-attach term, which would restore unbounded toggle frequency on the RealityKit callback slots.

testCases.name: testSentinelHoldMeasurementIncludesQueueWait
testCases.asserts: With the sentinel's measured hold exposed (`lastHoldSeconds`) or its clock injected: (a) enqueue a 250 ms blocking block onto the sentinel's own serial queue, then call `update(pixelBuffer:)` with a 32x32 buffer and wait for completion — assert lastHoldSeconds >= 0.25 and that the >100 ms path fired; (b) with the queue idle, call `update(pixelBuffer:)` on the same buffer — assert lastHoldSeconds < 0.10 and that the >100 ms path did NOT fire.
testCases.failsWhen: Case (a) fails on the round-2 build: `holdStart` is taken after dequeue, so the recorded value is only the perform() duration (single-digit ms on a 32x32 buffer) and the 100 ms branch never trips despite the buffer having been pinned for ~250 ms. Vacuity-proofed by case (b): a naive 'fix' that measures wall time from some fixed session origin, or that hardcodes a large value, fails the idle-queue row; and because (b) asserts the log does not fire, a fix that simply lowers the threshold also fails. Both rows assert on the same code path with opposite expected outcomes, so neither can pass by accident.

cleanAreas: MatteUniforms Swift↔Metal parity — verified mechanically field by field, not by eye: 28 members, identical order, identical widths, historyValid at byte offset 136 on both sides, size 156 / stride 160 matching the setBytes length. No padding divergence, no reordering.

RENDER-2 history correctness end to end — the ping-pong pairing means the shader's gated read at SemanticMatte.metal:243-244 can only ever touch a slot the previous dispatch fully wrote; the invalid seed path (previous = matte) produces smoothed == matte with no NaN reachable and biases toward MORE occlusion, so it cannot introduce draw-over. matteHistoryValid is read and written exclusively under stateLock.

bailOut coverage — encode() has exactly three returns and every one routes through bailOut; the post-encoder bail correctly ends the compute encoder before opening the blit encoder. No exit leaves inFlightTextures populated into the next frame.

prepare() race-discard — the probe/build/commit split is correct, the losing builder discards cleanly, the post-uninstall (pipeline nil, same device) case rebuilds rather than short-circuiting, and the commit is atomic w.r.t. encode.

SourceBox release semantics — nothing else retains the ARKit originals (the closure captures neither the ARFrame nor lidarSource), empty() precedes inference on every reachable path, and the one early guard above it destroys the box by destroying the closure context. The `busy` flag genuinely bounds the app to one in-flight capture buffer, including across the model-load window since `model` is published only at the end of the load closure.

Pooled copy under 5 Hz — pooled buffers are never published and are released at closure end, so the pool recycles rather than growing; the stride-mismatch branch copies at least the visible row bytes for both planes, so recycled padding garbage is never read back by Vision or by fitInverseDepth.

Lock-order invariant — held in practice, not just documented: encode takes stateLock then the feed locks; disarmSemanticMatte releases the feed lock before taking stateLock. No nesting in the forbidden direction anywhere in the pass or the session manager.

Texture binding hygiene in the kernel — every optional slot has a format-compatible 1x1 dummy and every dummy-backed read sits inside its own enable branch, so no dummy texture is ever sampled or has get_width() taken on it.

Mid-field sample freshness — 5 Hz publish (200 ms) against a 300 ms maxAge leaves no gap, and the snapshot's timestamp comparison uses the same ARFrame clock on both sides with a negative delta behaving correctly.

ARPCFG-3 tick ordering — updateWindowMode() and updatePowerTier() run in the same tick() pass, so moving the occlusion option to tick-derivation added zero latency to a window-mode or render-path edge.

reviews.lens: ARSession config + scheduling: tick-derived occlusion option, plan v2 truth table vs all consumers (request vs use, both directions), resume single-run claim, suspend reset completeness, grace-window / suspend-timer interactions.

closureVerdicts.item: ARPCFG-3/STATE-2 (tick-derived occlusion option; transitions set only their own flags)
closureVerdicts.trace: GeoARSessionManager.swift:1182-1193 derives the option every tick from the pure predicate at :1307-1311. setWindowMode (:1072-1081) and applyRenderPathIfNeeded (:1476+, transit branch, diff lines 364-384) no longer touch sceneUnderstanding.options — the edge-toggled restore that read the live `occlusionActive` is gone. Ordering verified safe: tick() runs applyRenderPathIfNeeded (:1016) then updateWindowMode (:1017) then updatePowerTier (:1018), so a render-path or window-mode transition has its option applied in the SAME tick, not the next. Self-blinding checked and refuted: updateWindowMode's pane probe (:1055-1059) raycasts mask .sceneUnderstanding, which is fed by the `.collision` option inserted at :765 and never removed — so turning `.occlusion` off in window mode cannot starve the probe that would turn window mode back off. Residual (not a finding, no traced harm): the write at :1189/:1191 is unconditional, so RealityKit's ARView.Environment setter is driven 2.5x/s with an identical value; a `contains` guard would make it free.

closureVerdicts.item: ARPCFG-1 (mid-field depth term = the consumer's real predicate; shared midFieldServiceable)
closureVerdicts.trace: REQUEST side closed: perceptionPlan's depth leg (:1284-1289) now carries midFieldServiceable + fullTier + pedestrian + !thermalSerious, and updatePowerTier feeds it via the shared static (:1101, :1297-1300). USE side did NOT adopt the shared predicate: frameUpdate:2409-2417 re-inlines `distance > midDepthMinContentDistance && distance < midDepthLiDARBandMax*midDepthSupportMargin`. The band arithmetic is numerically identical today, so no band divergence — but the doc comment at :1293-1296 claims 'the ONE predicate shared by the request side and the use side (frameUpdate's mid-depth gate)', and frameUpdate never calls it. The use gate is also missing three request-side terms: supportsSceneDepth, cameraVisible and !windowModeActive. supportsSceneDepth is reachable and harmful — see finding ARPCFG-R2-3. !windowModeActive is a real request<use inversion but I could not reach it: window mode requires nearestDrop > 15 m (:1049) and nearestDrop is the global nearest (:1541-1570), so a holder inside the 4-5 m band contradicts it in the common case; reported as a residual, not a finding.

closureVerdicts.item: ARPCFG-2 (suspend resets the scheduler; resume computes its own plan; sessionRunSince stamped)

Latent gap noted, not a finding: runGeoTracking:634-643 is the one session.run site that does not stamp sessionRunSince, harmless only because frameUpdate guards mode == .gpsCompass and appleGeoAnchorsEnabled is off.

findings.title: Reconstruction grace expires BEFORE the suspend it exists to cover — the tab-flip fires a mesh-destroying session.run ~0.2 s before session.pause()
findings.trace: The plan's grace clock and the holder's suspend timer use the same 5 s constant but start at different instants. lastCameraVisibleAt is written ONLY at :1092, inside updatePowerTier, which runs from the 400 ms tick loop (:981-989) — so it is quantized to the last TICK that saw the camera. The suspend timer starts at cameraDidDisappear (ARSessionHolder.swift:109-119, Task.sleep(AppConfig.pauseGraceSeconds), AppConfig.swift:150 = 5). Let phi in [0, 0.4) be the delay from the last visible tick to cameraDidDisappear. Ticks after the hide land at t = 0.4k - phi; the grace test at :1151-1152 is `now - lastCameraVisibleAt < 5`, i.e. it fails first at 0.4k >= 5, k = 13, t = 5.2 - phi. That tick precedes the suspend at t = 5 whenever phi > 0.2 — roughly half the phase space, and deterministic for a given exit phase. On that tick plan.reconstruction (:1271-1274) flips false; reconstruction is NOT hysteresis-damped (:1173 passes plan.reconstruction raw, applyPerceptionHysteresis at :1317 only wraps person/depth), so setPerception (:791-805) immediately runs makeConfiguration with sceneReconstruction left at .none (:667-669) — ARKit discards every ARMeshAnchor. 200 ms later suspendSession pauses. On resume, resumePlan re-requests .mesh (:488-500) and the mesh must rebuild from zero. Same mechanism hits the sub-5 s return that ARPCFG-4 was written for: the drop at t=4.85 plus the re-request at the next tick after cameraDidAppear = two session.runs and a full rebuild for a 4.9 s flip. WaveDTests.swift:179-188 cannot catch this — it hands the pure function `cameraRecentlyVisible: true` as a literal and never exercises the caller's clock.
findings.harm: Charter bar 'zero draw-over' is violated on the app's most common interaction. The tick-derived option keeps `.occlusion` inserted throughout (:1183-1192 — capable && pedestrian && !window, no reconstruction term), so RealityKit is asked to occlude with no mesh: for the seconds LiDAR takes to remesh after every tab flip, content renders straight through walls, furniture and the ground. The build's own comment at :660-662 states this cost ('every re-enable rebuilds the mesh from nothing, leaving a multi-second occlusion hole while sceneUnderstanding still requests occlusion'). Secondary: one extra full ARSession reconfiguration, i.e. a capture-pipeline restart and dropped frames, fired 0-200 ms before a pause that made it pointless.
findings.fix: Give the plan's grace strictly more room than the suspend timer plus one tick quantum. Either stamp `lastCameraVisibleAt = Date()` inside markCameraHidden() (GeoARSessionManager.swift:512-518) so the clock starts at the true visibility edge, or compare against a named `reconstructionGraceSeconds = AppConfig.pauseGraceSeconds + tickPeriodSeconds` at :1152. Expose tickPeriodSeconds as a static so the relationship is assertable.

findings.title: resumeSession's plan omits the camera-visibility term the tick's plan has — a warm-up resume fires two session.runs back to back
findings.trace: resumePlan (:488-494) is reconstruction = supportsSceneReconstruction && renderPath == .pedestrian && thermalState != .critical. perceptionPlan's reconstruction (:1271-1274) is the same three terms AND cameraRecentlyVisible. On the tab-flip path the divergence is masked: ARSessionHolder.cameraDidAppear (:61-66) calls startIfNeeded() then markCameraVisible() in one synchronous main-actor turn, and startTicking()'s Task body (:983-988) cannot run until a later turn, so the first tick already sees cameraVisible = true. beginRevealWarmup (ARSessionHolder.swift:55-59) calls startIfNeeded() and NEVER calls markCameraVisible — reachable from ReceiveScreen.swift:50 and OnboardingView.swift:154 whenever the user has already used the camera this run and the 5 s pause elapsed (attached == true, sessionRunning == false, so :104 takes resumeSession). There: run #1 at :496 applies reconstruction = true; the first tick, milliseconds later, sees cameraVisible = false and lastCameraVisibleAt at least 5 s stale, so plan.reconstruction = false, appliedPerception differs, and setPerception (:793-799) issues run #2. Deterministic, not phase-dependent. The comment at :482-487 ('the common resume is exactly ONE run') is false on this path.
findings.harm: Two full ARSession reconfigurations, each restarting the capture pipeline, at exactly the moment beginRevealWarmup exists to have a live session ready for 'Reveal in AR' — the pre-warm the call buys is thrown away and restarted twice. Both runs re-stamp sessionRunSince (:505, :803), so ADR-043's reveal gate (frameUpdate:2360-2366, frame.timestamp > sessionRunSince) must wait for a frame captured after the SECOND restart, adding restart latency to the reveal the warm-up was meant to remove. LiDAR scene reconstruction is also spun up and torn down within one tick while the camera surface is off-screen.
findings.fix: Make the resume plan the same function as the tick plan: give resumeSession a `cameraRecentlyVisible` input (cameraVisible || Date().timeIntervalSince(lastCameraVisibleAt) < grace) and require it for reconstruction, or extract `resumePerceptionPlan(...)` as a nonisolated static and assert it agrees with perceptionPlan's reconstruction for identical inputs.

findings.title: Mid-field depth USE gate has no capability term — the ~50 MB Depth Anything model loads on non-LiDAR devices that can never feed it
findings.trace: attach() computes the capability correctly at :365-366 (`wantsMidDepth = midFieldDepthEnabled && supportsFrameSemantics(.sceneDepth)`) and passes `midDepthFeed: wantsMidDepth ? midDepth.feed : nil` (:374) — so on a non-LiDAR device the pass holds a nil feed and can never consume a sample. But the consumer gate in frameUpdate is `if AppConfig.midFieldDepthEnabled, semanticPass != nil` (:2401), and semanticPass is non-nil whenever AppConfig.vpsEnabled alone is true (:367). The `useful` expression at :2411-2417 then checks only renderPath, thermalSerious, powerTier and the distance band — no supportsSceneDepth. So on any non-LiDAR iPhone with a drop 4-5 m away, camera up, tier .full, pedestrian, `useful` is true and :2421 calls midDepth.loadIfNeeded(), which decodes DepthAnythingV2SmallF16.mlmodelc with computeUnits = .all (MidFieldDepthEstimator.swift:104-126). Every subsequent update() bails at :141 (`frame.sceneDepth?.depthMap` is nil because plan.depth is false on that hardware, :1284), so the model can never produce a sample, and the pass could not read it if it did. This is the same capability-faithfulness gap ARPCFG-7 closed on the request side; the use side was not touched by round 2 (no diff hunk at :2401-2426).
findings.harm: A CoreML/ANE compile heat spike plus roughly 50 MB of model weights resident for the rest of the session, on the non-LiDAR majority of the install base, for a stream the hardware cannot deliver and a consumer that is nil. The ADR-035 comment at :2419-2420 names this exact cost ('the CoreML/ANE compile is a launch heat spike — pay it only when far content actually exists'). It lands during the .full tier with content in view, i.e. the hottest moment, against the charter's 'not thermal .serious at 10 min' bar.
findings.fix: Store `wantsMidDepth` from :365-366 as a property and gate :2401 on it (or on `semanticPass.hasMidDepthFeed`). While there, replace the inlined band at :2415-2416 with the shared Self.midFieldServiceable(distance:) so the doc claim at :1293-1296 becomes true, and add !windowModeActive so the use side is a subset of the request side in every term.

testCases.name: testReconstructionSurvivesEveryTickPhaseUpToTheSuspend
testCases.asserts: Sweep the hide phase phi over [0, 0.4) in 0.05 s steps. For each phi, simulate the tick schedule t_k = 0.4k - phi for all k with t_k < AppConfig.pauseGraceSeconds (every tick that runs BEFORE ARSessionHolder's suspend), compute the grace predicate the caller uses (now: t_k, lastCameraVisibleTickAt: -phi) and feed it to GeoARSessionManager.perceptionPlan with cameraVisible: false and everything else nominal (pedestrian, supportsSceneReconstruction, not critical). Assert .reconstruction is true for EVERY such tick, with the failing phi and t_k in the message. Add a companion assert that the grace constant exceeds AppConfig.pauseGraceSeconds by at least one tick period. Requires hoisting the :1151-1152 expression into a nonisolated static (cameraRecentlyVisible(cameraVisible:lastVisibleAt:now:)) and exposing tickPeriodSeconds — both pure, no ARKit.
testCases.failsWhen: Fails today at phi = 0.25/0.30/0.35 (tick t_13 = 5.2 - phi lands at 4.95/4.90/4.85 s, elapsed 5.2 s >= the 5 s grace) — exactly the session.run that destroys the mesh before the pause. Non-vacuous in both directions: the phi = 0.00-0.20 rows pass on today's code, so the test is not asserting a constant-false; and if the grace were widened to infinity the companion constant assert still pins it to one tick period rather than an arbitrary number. It also fails if someone later reverts lastCameraVisibleAt to tick-only stamping while keeping the widened constant, because the sweep is driven by the tick schedule, not by the constant.

testCases.name: testResumePlanAgreesWithTheFirstTickPlan
testCases.asserts: Extract resumeSession's tuple (:488-494) as `nonisolated static func resumePerceptionPlan(supportsSceneReconstruction:pedestrian:thermalCritical:cameraRecentlyVisible:)`. For both values of cameraRecentlyVisible (true and false), with supportsSceneReconstruction: true, pedestrian: true, thermalCritical: false, assert resumePerceptionPlan(...).reconstruction == perceptionPlan(...).reconstruction where perceptionPlan is called with the state the first post-resume tick actually sees (tierAboveIdle: false, fullTier: false, cameraVisible: same value, cameraRecentlyVisible: same value, personLikely: false, contentInViewRecently: false, midFieldServiceable: false, thermals false, all capabilities true). Also assert person and depth are false in both, so the resume never raises a fast stream.
testCases.failsWhen: Fails today on the cameraRecentlyVisible: false row: resumePlan yields reconstruction = true while the first tick's plan yields false — the two session.runs of the beginRevealWarmup path. Non-vacuous: the cameraRecentlyVisible: true row passes on today's code (both true), so the assertion is not trivially failing, and it would catch the opposite regression too — if someone made the resume plan unconditionally false, the true row breaks. Pinning tierAboveIdle/fullTier/personLikely to the values a first tick really has (governor state and sentinel evidence both cold) is what makes the comparison a claim about the real transition rather than about two arbitrary calls.

testCases.name: testMidFieldUseIsASubsetOfTheMidFieldRequest
testCases.asserts: Extract frameUpdate's :2411-2417 gate as `nonisolated static func midFieldDepthUseful(enabled:supportsSceneDepth:pedestrian:thermalSerious:fullTier:anyServiceable:windowModeActive:)`. Exhaustively enumerate all 2^7 input combinations; for each, if midFieldDepthUseful(...) is true then assert perceptionPlan(...) with the matching terms (personLikely: false so the mid-field leg is the only depth claimant, cameraVisible: true, midFieldEnabled/midFieldServiceable/pedestrian/thermalSerious/fullTier/supportsSceneDepth/windowModeActive mirrored) returns depth == true. Add two explicit anchors: midFieldDepthUseful(supportsSceneDepth: false, everything else favourable) == false, and midFieldDepthUseful(all favourable) == true.
testCases.failsWhen: Fails today on every combination with supportsSceneDepth = false and the band/tier/path favourable — the use side says run (loading the 50 MB model) while the request side says the hardware has no depth — and on windowModeActive = true for the same reason. Non-vacuous: the all-favourable anchor asserts a true, so a predicate hardwired to false fails; the exhaustive implication would also catch the reverse over-tightening (a use gate narrower than needed still passes, which is correct — the invariant being pinned is use ⊆ request, the exact direction ARPCFG-1 was raised about). Because the enumeration is exhaustive rather than a hand-picked table, adding a term to one side without the other breaks it automatically.

cleanAreas: Tick-derived occlusion option ordering: tick() runs applyRenderPathIfNeeded → updateWindowMode → updatePowerTier (GeoARSessionManager.swift:1016-1018), so a window-mode or render-path transition has its sceneUnderstanding option applied in the same tick — no one-tick lag, and the two round-1 interleavings that stranded the option removed are structurally gone.

The window-mode probe cannot self-blind: updateWindowMode's pane raycast uses mask .sceneUnderstanding (:1055-1059), which is backed by the `.collision` option inserted at :765 and never removed by the tick derivation — turning `.occlusion` off in window mode leaves the evidence path that would turn it back off fully intact.

Perception hysteresis is correctly scoped: applyPerceptionHysteresis (:1317-1337) wraps only person and depth; reconstruction is passed raw (:1173), so the stateful axis is never held up by a 10 s timer and the fast axes never cycle session.run on the 400 ms tick. During the 5 s pause grace the 10 s person/depth hysteresis holds both applied, so the grace window itself produces no fast-axis reconfiguration.

setPerception's tuple-equality guard (:793) plus the capability terms now inside the plan means no-op runs are impossible for the hardware-lacks-it case that round 1 flagged; sessionRunSince is stamped at every reachable run site (:473, :505, :781, :803).

RENDER-2 uniform layout: all 28 fields of Swift MatteUniforms (SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:105-146) and Metal MatteUniforms (SemanticMatte.metal:14-49) agree field-for-field and in size; historyValid is false on every (re)alloc and true only after a dispatch has written the texture the next frame reads.

RENDER-1's non-clearing passIdleSince is harmless because setCallbacksActive is change-guarded (SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:186-206) — the repeated detach calls every 400 ms are a lock-and-return, not a repeated cross-thread mutation of the callback slots.

RENDER-5's SourceBox genuinely releases pre-inference: MidFieldDepthEstimator.swift:163 empties the box before the VNImageRequestHandler is constructed at :173, so ARKit's pool buffers are held only for the two memcpys.

Mid-field sample staleness is safe across a suspend: the consumer snapshots with maxAge 0.3 s against the frame timestamp (SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:314-315), so a sample surviving suspendSession expires on the first post-resume encode rather than matting against stale geometry.

suspendSession's reset covers the scheduler state that matters (appliedPerception, both hysteresis clocks, the live-edit capture, semantic matte disarm, failure/interruption holds, tick cancellation). windowModeActive, passIdleSince and midDepthActive survive the pause but all self-correct within the first post-resume tick or frame, and the session is not rendering while paused.

findings.title: The 1.5 s gesture terminator fires on a stationary-finger drag and lets the still-live gesture re-bind to a different drop, persisting the edit
findings.trace: The terminator is time-based only: GeoARSessionManager.swift:1088-1091 `if editingDropID != nil, Date().timeIntervalSince(lastLiveEditTickAt) > 1.5 { cancelLiveEdit() }`. Its only clock source is a slider VALUE CHANGE — GeoARSessionManager.swift:1893 `if !commit { lastLiveEditTickAt = Date() }`. ARScreen's three sliders wire nothing to gesture BEGIN: ARScreen.swift:489-502, :510-523, :531-544 pass only `{ editing in if !editing { ...commit... } }`, so touch-down and finger-held-still produce zero calls. A finger resting on the thumb for 1.5 s therefore looks identical to a torn-down cover. cancelLiveEdit (GeoARSessionManager.swift:442-446) then clears BOTH `liveEditingDrops` and `editingDropID` while the touch is still down — and, critically, does NOT clear `nearestDrop`, so the adjust panel (gated on `manager.nearestDrop != nil` at ARScreen.swift:289) stays mounted and the Slider view is never destroyed. With `editingDropID` nil, updateNearest unfreezes (GeoARSessionManager.swift:1545) and on the next 400 ms tick can select a different drop; ARScreen.swift:583 `.onChange(of: manager.nearestDrop?.id) { syncSliders() }` then rewrites liveHeight/liveScale/liveRotation under the finger. The next finger movement re-enters adjustNearestDrop with editingDropID nil and re-captures at GeoARSessionManager.swift:1891 `editingDropID = nearestDrop?.id` — now the WRONG drop. Release commits it: GeoARSessionManager.swift:1949-1962 `library.update(edited, persist: true)` → DropStore.swift:916-932 writes disk and enqueues cloud sync. This is the SWE-5 defect (GeoARSessionManager.swift:232-238 documents it as fixed) reopened through the new terminator.
findings.harm: Two concrete harms in a session with ≥2 drops near each other (the common 'I left two gifts here' case, and the two-object Playground flow which resolves nearest by AR-space distance at GeoARSessionManager.swift:1548-1560). (1) Wrong-drop persist: user drags drop A's height slider, holds still ~1.9 s to look up and judge the placement — the designed interaction, per the panel's own doc comment at ARScreen.swift:481-483 'slide size while looking at it' — then finishes the drag; drop B's height/scale/facing is silently overwritten on disk and pushed to Firestore, and drop A is left unchanged. (2) Positioners fight the finger: `liveEditingDrops.removeAll()` re-exposes the drag target to applyVPSTransform, whose guard at GeoARSessionManager.swift:860 ('Never fight the user's finger mid-slide') no longer holds — a VPS-owned drop gets yanked to its terrain-anchor height mid-gesture — and to syncGPSPlacements' absolute-y recompute at GeoARSessionManager.swift:1717-1762, which disagrees with the relative `holder.position.y += Float(height - oldHeight)` the slider applies at :1918, producing a visible jump under the finger.
findings.fix: Make the terminator key on gesture LIVENESS, not tick cadence. Add `onEditingChanged` begin/end plumbing: in ARScreen.swift:498-502/:519-523/:540-544 change each closure to `{ editing in if editing { manager.beginLiveEdit() } else { manager.adjustNearestDrop(..., commit: true) } }`, have beginLiveEdit() stamp lastLiveEditTickAt, and gate the terminator on `!gestureTouchActive`. Extract the decision as a pure `static func liveEditVerdict(captureExists:gestureTouchActive:sinceLastTick:) -> LiveEditVerdict` so it is table-testable. Belt-and-braces: in adjustNearestDrop, refuse to re-capture a DIFFERENT id while a touch is still active — if the capture was cleared under a live gesture, drop the remaining ticks instead of rebinding.

findings.title: The mesh-build budget is per sync pass, and sync passes run at render rate — the claimed backlog bound does not bind
findings.trace: GeospatialEngine.swift:444-447 declares `meshBuildBudgetPerPass = 8` with the stated invariant 'the rest re-offer on later frames instead of pinning N vertex buffers in a backlog'. The admission at :467-468 applies `.prefix(8)` to the per-pass `pending` list and consults `meshBuildsInFlight` only to skip ids ALREADY queued (:461) — it never caps total outstanding work, so each pass admits 8 NEW ids on top of everything still queued. syncOccluders is called from GeospatialEngine.swift:239-241 inside `update(with:)`, which the render loop drives at `garFeedInterval` — GeoARSessionManager.swift:2383-2386. During a VPS convergence sprint that interval is literally 0 (GeoARSessionManager.swift:1356-1357 `interval = elapsed < 20 ? 0 : ...`), so update runs on every SceneEvents.Update tick (~60 Hz), i.e. up to 480 admissions/second; even settled, GeoARSessionManager.swift:1364-1366 gives 15 Hz (full) or 10 Hz (cruise) = 120/80 admissions per second. Every admitted closure retains its GARStreetscapeGeometry for the whole time it sits on the serial `meshQueue` (:429, comment at :472-473 makes the retention explicit).
findings.harm: On the exact scenario the fix names — a corner turn streaming a dense block while VPS is still converging (localized but above vpsGoodHorizontalAccuracy, so isConverging is true and the sprint interval is 0) — the entire streamed building set reaches the serial queue within ⌈N/8⌉ render frames, ~200 ms for N=100. All N GARStreetscapeGeometry vertex+triangle buffers are then pinned simultaneously by queued closures while a single .userInitiated thread runs MeshResource.generate back to back. The pre-fix and post-fix peak memory are the same; only the time to reach it changed. Reviewers reading GeospatialEngine.swift:444-447 will believe the backlog is bounded at 8 when the real bound is N.
findings.fix: Make the budget a CONCURRENCY cap rather than a per-pass cap: admit `max(0, budget - meshBuildsInFlight.count)` ids per pass, and extract the choice as a pure `static func meshBuildAdmissions(pending:inFlight:budget:) -> [UUID]` so the bound is table-testable. Optionally also rate-limit syncOccluders itself (it does not need to run at 60 Hz — the already-built occluders' setTransformMatrix loop at :457-459 is the only part that benefits from render-rate updates).

findings.title: Re-prime advances every drop's watermark but surfaces only one reaction — simultaneous missed reactions are permanently swallowed
findings.trace: ReactionService.swift:171-191 is the re-prime branch. For each listener it assigns the missed reaction to the single @Published slot at :184-185 (`self.incoming = reaction; self.incomingDropTitle = title`) and then unconditionally advances the durable watermark at :188 `self.recordSeen(key: key, reactionID: doc.documentID)`, which persists to UserDefaults at :48-49. listenToMySharedDrops attaches up to 10 listeners (watchedDrops cap at :109-111), and the re-attach path fires them all at once — RootView.swift:247-256 calls stop() on .background (clearing `primedListeners` at :257) and listenToMySharedDrops() on .active, so every one of the 10 listeners re-primes in the same foreground burst. Each callback hops through `Task { @MainActor }` (:156) and overwrites `incoming`; RootView.swift:64 renders exactly one. There is no queue: `clearIncoming()` (:249-252) nils the slot rather than popping a next.
findings.harm: Sender has 3 shared drops; a reaction lands on each while the app is backgrounded. On foreground return, all 3 re-prime: 3 watermarks advance to the new document ids, and 1 toast renders (the last callback to land — the other two assignments are overwritten within the same run-loop turn, so SwiftUI never draws them). The other 2 reactions are now permanently unrecoverable: the durable watermark equals their id, so :180 `doc.documentID != known` is false on every future re-prime, and the live path (:192-200) only fires on new `.added` changes. This is exactly the class of loss STATE-6 was built to close, on the plural case — and STATE-6 made it durable, because before round 2 the swallow was silent-but-repairable-by-a-later-reaction and now the watermark records the swallow.
findings.fix: Buffer instead of overwriting. Add `private var missedQueue: [(key: String, title: String, reaction: DropReaction)]`; in the re-prime branch enqueue rather than assign, and record the watermark only when an entry is actually surfaced. Make `clearIncoming()` pop the next queued entry into `incoming` (and record ITS watermark) instead of nilling unconditionally, so N missed reactions produce N sequential toasts and N watermark advances. Extract the enqueue/pop reducer as a pure static so it is unit-testable without Firestore.

findings.title: ARPCFG-1's capability term landed on the request side only — frameUpdate loads the ~50 MB depth model on hardware where it can never produce a sample
findings.trace: perceptionPlan's depth term now carries `supportsSceneDepth` (GeoARSessionManager.swift:1284) and the shared predicate exists at :1297-1300. The USE side was never touched (no hunk for it in `git diff dec7a6a~1 dec7a6a`): GeoARSessionManager.swift:2409-2422 open-codes the band and its `useful` expression is `renderPath == .pedestrian && !thermalSerious && powerTier == .full && <some drop in 4–5 m>` — no capability term, and it does not call Self.midFieldServiceable. The enclosing guard is `if AppConfig.midFieldDepthEnabled, semanticPass != nil` (:2401), and the pass is constructed whenever `AppConfig.vpsEnabled || wantsPersonOcclusion || wantsMidDepth` (:367) — so on a non-LiDAR phone with a VPS key present, semanticPass is non-nil while `wantsMidDepth` (:365-366, gated on supportsFrameSemantics(.sceneDepth)) is false and `midDepthFeed` was passed as nil (:374). `useful` then goes true and :2421 calls `midDepth.loadIfNeeded()`, which decodes DepthAnythingV2SmallF16 — 'about 50 MB of weights' per MidFieldDepthEstimator.swift:96 — into a VNCoreMLModel with computeUnits .all (:104-126). Every subsequent `midDepth.update(frame:hz:)` then dies on the `guard let lidarSource = frame.sceneDepth?.depthMap` at MidFieldDepthEstimator.swift:141-144, so the model can never publish a sample.
findings.harm: On every non-LiDAR iPhone (the majority of the install base) running a shipping build with a Google Geospatial key, the first time any drop sits 4–5 m away at full tier the app pays a CoreML/ANE compile — the launch-class heat spike ADR-035 explicitly defers — and then holds ~50 MB of model weights resident for the whole session, feeding a MidFieldDepthFeed the render pass was not even wired to. That is pure memory footprint against the crash-free 99.5 % bar plus a one-shot thermal cost, for a feature that is structurally incapable of producing output on that hardware. The underlying gate is unchanged from round 1 — I am filing it because the charter asked me to verify the use side and because the round-2 commit message now asserts 'shared static with the use side', which is not true in either direction (no call, no capability term).
findings.fix: Route both sides through one predicate. Add `nonisolated static func midFieldUseful(supportsSceneDepth:pedestrian:thermalSerious:fullTier:anyServiceable:) -> Bool`, call it from frameUpdate (replacing :2411-2417) and use it as the mid-field clause of perceptionPlan's depth term (:1287-1288). At minimum, add `ARWorldTrackingConfiguration.supportsFrameSemantics(.sceneDepth)` to the `useful` expression so loadIfNeeded() is unreachable without LiDAR. Also consider gating the `midDepthActive` HUD chip (:1387) on the same capability so DPT cannot light on hardware that lacks the alignment source.

findings.title: The durable reaction watermark dictionary is never pruned — it grows monotonically in UserDefaults for the life of the install
findings.trace: ReactionService.swift:37 declares `lastSeenReactionIDs: [String: String]`, keyed by drop UUID string, hydrated from UserDefaults.standard at :41-44 and re-serialized in full on every write at :48-49 `UserDefaults.standard.set(lastSeenReactionIDs, forKey:)`. The only prune in the class is the listener prune at :143-147, which removes entries from `listeners` and `primedListeners` for drops that left the shared set — it deliberately does not touch `lastSeenReactionIDs`. `stop()` (:254-258) also leaves it alone, correctly (it is meant to be durable). Nothing removes a key when a drop is deleted (DropStore.swift:935-979 `remove` has no hook into ReactionService), unshared, or made private, so keys accumulate for every drop the user has ever shared.
findings.harm: A prolific sender accumulates one permanent ~36-byte key plus a ~36-byte value (plus plist overhead) for every drop they have ever link-shared, and the whole dictionary is re-encoded and written to the standard defaults domain on the main actor on every single reaction recorded (:49, reached from both the prime path :188 and the live path :196). At a few hundred drops this is tens of KB re-serialized per reaction — not a frame-budget killer today, but an unbounded growth curve in a durable store with no upper bound and no expiry, and it is newly introduced by round 2.
findings.fix: Prune inside the existing loop at ReactionService.swift:143-147 using the SAME `allSharedKeys` set the listener prune uses (so the SURF-lens-4 rule holds: a drop that merely fell out of the newest-10 attach window keeps its watermark; only a drop that left the shared set entirely loses it). Extract as `nonisolated static func prunedWatermarks(_ current: [String: String], keepingSharedKeys: Set<String>) -> [String: String]` and write once per listen pass only when the result differs.

testCases.name: testStationaryFingerDoesNotTerminateALiveGesture
testCases.asserts: Table-test the extracted pure terminator `GeoARSessionManager.liveEditVerdict(captureExists:gestureTouchActive:sinceLastTick:)`. Rows: (true, gestureTouchActive: true, 3.0) -> .keep — a finger still on the thumb is a live gesture no matter how long it has been still; (true, gestureTouchActive: false, 3.0) -> .cancel — a torn-down cover with no touch abandons; (true, gestureTouchActive: false, 0.5) -> .keep — inside the dwell, still pending; (false, gestureTouchActive: true, 99.0) -> .keep — no capture, nothing to terminate. Paired assertion on the re-capture guard: `editTarget(existing: nil, nearest: dropB, gestureTouchActive: true)` returns nil (refuse to rebind mid-gesture) while `editTarget(existing: nil, nearest: dropB, gestureTouchActive: false)` returns dropB.
testCases.failsWhen: Vacuity-proofed in both directions. The current build's rule is `sinceLastTick > 1.5 -> cancel` with no touch term, so row 1 returns .cancel and the test FAILS on today's code (GeoARSessionManager.swift:1088-1091). Row 2 forbids the trivial 'always .keep' pass; row 3 forbids 'cancel whenever there is no touch'; row 4 forbids ignoring captureExists. The editTarget pair forbids a fix that only lengthens the dwell without closing the rebind.

testCases.name: testMeshAdmissionsRespectTotalOutstandingWork
testCases.asserts: Table-test the extracted pure `GeospatialEngine.meshBuildAdmissions(pending:inFlight:budget:)`. Case A: 30 pending at increasing distances, inFlight = 8, budget = 8 -> returns []. Case B: same 30 pending, inFlight = 0, budget = 8 -> returns exactly the 8 nearest ids, in ascending-distance order. Case C: same 30 pending, inFlight = 5, budget = 8 -> returns exactly 3 ids, and they are the 3 nearest. Case D: 2 pending, inFlight = 0, budget = 8 -> returns both (a small block is not throttled).
testCases.failsWhen: Case A FAILS on today's code: GeospatialEngine.swift:467-468 applies `.prefix(8)` to `pending` with no reference to `meshBuildsInFlight.count`, so it admits 8 more on top of the 8 already queued. Cases B and D forbid the trivial 'always return []' pass; case B's ordering assertion forbids dropping the nearest-first sort while fixing the cap; case C forbids an all-or-nothing gate that admits either a full batch or nothing.

testCases.name: testEveryMissedReactionSurfacesBeforeItsWatermarkAdvances
testCases.asserts: Drive the re-prime reducer with three keys, each carrying a newest document id that differs from its stored watermark, delivered back to back with no intervening dismissal. Assert: (1) after the burst, exactly one reaction is in `incoming` and exactly ONE watermark has advanced — the other two are still queued and still hold their OLD watermark; (2) two `clearIncoming()` calls surface the second and third reactions in arrival order, each advancing its own watermark as it is surfaced; (3) after the third dismissal `incoming` is nil, the queue is empty, and all three watermarks equal the three new document ids; (4) a fourth key whose newest document id EQUALS its stored watermark is never enqueued and never surfaces.
testCases.failsWhen: Assertion (1) FAILS on today's code — ReactionService.swift:188 advances all three watermarks during the burst while :184 leaves only one reaction in the slot — and assertion (2) FAILS because clearIncoming() (:249-252) nils the slot with nothing to pop. Assertion (4) is the vacuity guard against a fix that simply toasts every initial-snapshot row (which would re-toast history on every foreground return); assertion (3) is the guard against a fix that queues but never drains.

testCases.name: testMidFieldRequestAndUseAgreeIncludingCapability
testCases.asserts: Over the full cross product of (supportsSceneDepth, pedestrian, thermalSerious, fullTier, anyServiceable), assert the symmetry the ARPCFG-1 fix claims: `midFieldUseful(...) == false` for every input where perceptionPlan's mid-field clause is false, and specifically that `midFieldUseful(supportsSceneDepth: false, pedestrian: true, thermalSerious: false, fullTier: true, anyServiceable: true) == false`. Plus two positive rows so the predicate is not vacuously false: (supportsSceneDepth: true, pedestrian: true, thermalSerious: false, fullTier: true, anyServiceable: true) == true, and flipping anyServiceable to false -> false. Plus a band-agreement row proving the use side calls the shared static: `midFieldServiceable(distance: 4.5) == true` and `midFieldServiceable(distance: 5.5) == false` are the SAME values the use-side gate produces for a holder at those distances.
testCases.failsWhen: The no-capability row FAILS today because frameUpdate's `useful` expression (GeoARSessionManager.swift:2411-2417) contains no supportsSceneDepth term, so it evaluates true on a non-LiDAR device with a drop at 4.5 m — the state that reaches `midDepth.loadIfNeeded()` at :2421. The two positive rows forbid a fix that hard-codes false; the band rows forbid a fix that adds the capability term while leaving the band expression duplicated (they only hold if the use side routes through Self.midFieldServiceable).

testCases.name: testWatermarksPruneOnlyForDropsThatLeftTheSharedSet
testCases.asserts: Table-test `ReactionService.prunedWatermarks(_:keepingSharedKeys:)`. Case A: three stored watermarks, sharedKeys contains only the first -> result has exactly that one key with its value intact. Case B: three stored watermarks, sharedKeys contains all three -> result is unchanged (all three keys, same values). Case C: a key that is in sharedKeys but OUTSIDE the newest-10 attach window (i.e. present in `sharedDrops` but absent from `watchedDrops`) is KEPT — mirroring the SURF-lens-4 rule the listener prune already honours at ReactionService.swift:140-147. Case D: empty sharedKeys -> empty result.
testCases.failsWhen: There is no such function today and nothing prunes ReactionService.swift:37, so case A fails immediately. Case B is the vacuity guard against 'always return [:]'; case C is the guard against pruning on `watchedDrops` (the newest-10 attach window) instead of `sharedDrops`, which would silently destroy the watermark of every drop past the 10th and re-open the swallow STATE-6 exists to fix; case D pins the degenerate boundary.

cleanAreas: clearRoomDrops iteration safety (GeoARSessionManager.swift:604-613): removePerDropState touches sixteen per-drop maps but never `roomDrops`, so the `roomDrops.keys` view is not invalidated mid-iteration and the removeAll() at :610 is the only mutation. The two omissions of the old ad-hoc loop (editingDropID, revealedDrops) are covered at :1524 and :1528.

removePerDropState / invalidateAnchor re-request path (GeoARSessionManager.swift:1512-1539 + GeospatialEngine.swift:411-419): correct, not churn. requestedDrops/resolvedDrops/in-flight token are all cleared, and tickGPSCompass re-offers every eligible drop each tick (:1630-1634), so a returning drop re-pins on the next 400 ms tick. I probed the two plausible flapping sources and both are already closed: DropStore's refresh publish is explicitly additive in phase 1 (DropStore.swift:571-582, comment names 'tear down their AR entities' as the reason), and LocationService.location is never re-nilled after the first fix, so eligibleDrops cannot collapse to demoDrops mid-session.

stop() vs in-flight mesh landings (GeospatialEngine.swift:194-218, :474-506): fully safe. stop() clears meshBuildsInFlight and empties SeenGeometryBox before any queued closure can matter; the queue-side guard at :477 discards pre-extraction, and the main-hop guard at :497-499 re-checks occluders[id], seenGeometry and arView, so a landing that raced past the first check cannot install an orphan occluder or resurrect state into a stopped engine.

recordSeen on own reactions (ReactionService.swift:196-197): correct as written — the watermark is advanced BEFORE the `reaction.uid != myUid` early return, so a self-reaction cannot re-toast as 'missed' on the next re-prime. This is the right ordering and I found no path that skips it.

Mesh re-offer latency and far-building starvation (GeospatialEngine.swift:453-468): `pending` is rebuilt and re-sorted by live camera distance on every pass, so a deferred building returns 17–100 ms later and the nearest-first ordering is self-correcting as the viewer walks. No starvation.

cancelLiveEdit wiring (GeoARSessionManager.swift:434, :517; ARSessionHolder.swift:70, :76, :121-125): a drag genuinely cannot outlive its surface — cover dismissal routes through cameraDidDisappear→markCameraHidden, and backgrounding routes through appDidEnterBackground→suspend→suspendSession. FLOW-5's stated goal is met; only the tick-cadence terminator added alongside it is defective.

liveEditingDrops / editingDropID coupling: I traced every mutation site (GeoARSessionManager.swift:828-829, 442-446, 1900-1901, 1913, 1523-1524, 1965-1966) and found no path that leaves liveEditingDrops non-empty with editingDropID nil, so the governor's `.full` pin (:1116) cannot be stranded the way SWE-5 described.

suspendSession/resumeSession perception scheduler (GeoARSessionManager.swift:431-434, 488-507): the resume-computes-its-own-plan choice is sound. Reconstruction-only on resume is the right call — it is the stateful axis whose rebuild leaves an occlusion hole, while person/depth genuinely must re-earn from fresh frames because the sentinel's evidence decayed over the pause. Common resume is exactly one session.run; a second run happens only when a human is actually back in frame.

Occlusion-option derivation under interruption (GeoARSessionManager.swift:1014 + :1182-1193): the tick guard holds the derivation while interrupted/failed, which is correct — the option is left as-is rather than being churned against ARKit's own recovery, and the first healthy tick re-derives it.

reviews.lens: End-to-end presentation + UX. Verified against source at HEAD (build commit dec7a6a). Traced every flow named in the charter lens through the round-2 single-cover machine: RootView.swift (destinationBinding, coverContent, the two toast/banner instances, the phase→memory gate, the FLOW-4 camera-exit rule, the onOpenURL/sheet promotion pair), AppRouter.swift (linkArrived/promotePendingReceive/showCamera/beginFireworksDemo/finishOnboarding), OnboardingView.swift (router-held beat, Skip, startDemo), ARScreen.swift (chevron sibling, statusCard chips, adjust panel, snapshot hand-off), HomeScreen.swift (forYouCard/playgroundCard), MemoryScreen.swift, ReceiveScreen.swift, ReactionSession.swift, ReactionService.swift, CreateWizard.swift (exit + share-sheet loop), and the GeoARSessionManager surfaces those flows touch (showPersistError slot discipline, snapNearestDropToGround decline, clearRoomDrops/removePerDropState, cancelLiveEdit, occlusionOptionDesired/perceptionPlan/midFieldServiceable, resumeSession). One structural note on the presentation model that shaped several traces: .fullScreenCover has NO interactive dismissal, so every camera/onboarding/create exit is programmatic — the destinationBinding setter is reachable only from MemoryScreen's dismiss() and CreateWizard's dismiss(); its .camera/.onboardingStory cases are effectively dead but harmless because showCamera=false and finishOnboarding() do the same work. RENDER-1/2/3/4/5/6/7, RSCH-2, STATE-8 and the Metal/queue internals were left to the render and concurrency lenses and are deliberately absent from my closure table rather than guessed at. Verdict: three new MEDIUM defects, all introduced or newly made reachable by round-2 code; no blockers; no HIGH/CRITICAL I can defend with a concrete trace.

findings.title: Round 2's second, cover-scoped reaction toast makes an unguarded cancellation-clear reachable — any cover transition wipes a live toast, defeating FLOW-9
findings.harm: The sender's live reaction toast is the loop's payoff and its only surface — there is no reaction inbox, and ReactionService.incoming/incomingDropTitle are the sole carriers of the reactor's name and the drop title. Leaving any cover within 4 s of a toast destroys it mid-read, and the natural user response to seeing a toast in the camera IS to tap the chevron out to look at it. This is precisely the harm round-1 FLOW-9 was raised against ('the old auto-clear discarded the toast unseen'); round 2's fix for it reintroduces it in a new shape.
findings.fix: Guard the cancellation and key the window to the reaction: `.task(id: reaction.id) { do { try await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(4)) } catch { return }; reactionService.clearIncoming() }`. Better, since the toast is now rendered twice: move the timer out of the view entirely and give ReactionService a single owner — e.g. an `autoClearIncoming(after:)` started when `incoming` is assigned (ReactionService.swift:184 and :198) and cancelled/restarted per reaction — leaving both overlays as pure renderers with no lifecycle of their own.

findings.title: FLOW-10's Home card commits the full watch ritual at any distance — a one-tap path from the front door to a fabricated Memory and a false reaction to the sender
findings.harm: The sender is told their gift was found and reacted to by someone who was three kilometres away and never saw it, and the receiver is handed a keepsake asserting a live viewing that did not happen. This is a fabricated receipt in both directions, against the invariant the counsel has enforced across rounds 8/10/12 and that the code itself states at MemoryScreen.swift:57-58 ('Nothing on this screen fabricates a receipt') and :173-175. The received drop is also consumed as 'watched' with no way to redo the moment properly on arrival.
findings.fix: Make the card's action a function of distance, matching the copy it already renders. Introduce one pure seam, e.g. `static func watchAdmission(distanceMeters: Double?) -> WatchAdmission` returning `.startRitual` inside the arrival radius (the 60 m the subline already uses at HomeScreen.swift:182) and `.navigateOnly` otherwise and when there is no location fix; on `.navigateOnly` set `router.showCamera = true` WITHOUT startWatching, and let the ritual begin from the camera when the drop actually renders (manager.renderedDropCount > 0 / nearestDropDistance inside the radius). That keeps FLOW-10 closed for the case it was raised for while removing the fabricated-receipt path.

findings.title: ARPCFG-6's ground-snap decline was wired into the CRITICAL persist-error slot and evicts a live data-loss message from the adjacent control
findings.trace:
GeoARSessionManager.swift:2033-2039, added by round 2:

    guard let groundY else {
        showPersistError("Couldn't find the ground here — move closer and try again")
        return
    }

`showPersistError` defaults to `critical: true` (:93). The round-6 slot discipline at :94-96 only blocks a NON-critical message from evicting a critical one — a critical message always overwrites whatever is on screen and restarts the 4 s clear task (:99-105). Every other advisory-class call site correctly opts out: :353 and :1822 both pass `critical: false`. This new one does not, so a transient 'move closer' advisory now outranks and destroys data-loss warnings.

The eviction pair sits inside one panel. ARScreen.swift:484-573 adjustPanel: the three sliders commit on release (:500, :521, :542) into adjustNearestDrop, whose save failure fires `showPersistError("Couldn't save the change — it may revert")` at GeoARSessionManager.swift:1959 (critical). One row below the sliders is 'Place on ground' (ARScreen.swift:552-561) — and it is the DESIGNED follow-up, per the comment at :549-550 ('the slider's 0 uses the coarse ground estimate, which can hover'). So: user drags height → release → save fails → red 'Couldn't save the change — it may revert' appears in statusCard (ARScreen.swift:417-422) → user taps 'Place on ground' inches below within the 4 s window → no plane/mesh/estimate resolves (indoors on a non-LiDAR phone, or with reconstruction shed by transit/thermal/camera-grace, which the round-2 mesh gate at :2014-2027 makes more likely) → the decline overwrites the save-failure text and restarts its own clear task. The same eviction runs against the receive-path warning at RootView.swift:214-217 ('Couldn't save this drop — it may disappear after this session'), which fires seconds before the user lands in the camera with the received drop placed.
findings.harm: A data-loss warning is destroyed unseen by a cosmetic advisory triggered from the adjacent button, and the user is left believing an edit persisted (or that a received drop was saved) when it did not. persistErrorText is single-slot with no history, so the warning has no second surface. This regresses an invariant the counsel already made law in round 6 (sync-6/arui-6, encoded in the comment at :86-90).
findings.fix: `showPersistError("Couldn't find the ground here — move closer and try again", critical: false)`. Cleaner: give transient AR advisories their own published slot rather than borrowing the persist-failure channel, so an advisory can never contend with a data-loss message at all — the decline is a coaching message, not a failure to save.

testCases.name: testReactionToastTimerDoesNotClearOnCancellation
testCases.asserts: Requires the fix's seam: move the timer body out of the view into `ReactionService` as `@MainActor func autoClearIncoming(after seconds: Double) async` (the single-owner form the fix recommends), containing the same sleep-then-clear logic. Then, in AugmentMeRealityTests/WaveDTests.swift, three legs in one test. (a) CANCELLATION LEG: seed `service.incoming` with a DropReaction, start `let t = Task { await service.autoClearIncoming(after: 4) }`, await 50 ms, `t.cancel()`, await 50 ms, then `XCTAssertNotNil(service.incoming, "a cancelled toast timer must not clear a live reaction")`. (b) COMPLETION LEG (vacuity): seed `incoming` again, `await service.autoClearIncoming(after: 0.05)`, then `XCTAssertNil(service.incoming, "a timer that runs to completion must clear")`. (c) RESTART LEG (vacuity): seed reaction A, start the timer, at 30 ms assign reaction B (a different id) and assert that at 60 ms — i.e. past A's would-be deadline had it been shortened — `incoming?.id == B.id` and is still non-nil, pinning that a second reaction gets its own full window rather than inheriting A's.
testCases.failsWhen: Leg (a) FAILS against today's code: `try? await Task.sleep(...)` swallows CancellationError and `clearIncoming()` runs anyway, so `incoming` is nil at the assert. Vacuity is pinned from both sides — leg (b) fails if the fix degenerates into a timer that never clears (which would leave the toast on screen forever), and leg (c) fails if the fix keeps the un-keyed single-shot window (a second reaction cut short). No single degenerate implementation passes all three.

testCases.name: testHomeForYouTapRequiresArrivalBeforeStartingTheRitual
testCases.asserts: Requires the fix's seam: a pure `static func watchAdmission(distanceMeters: Double?, arrivalRadius: Double) -> WatchAdmission` (`.startRitual` / `.navigateOnly`) that HomeScreen.forYouCard's action calls. Four legs. (a) FAR: `watchAdmission(distanceMeters: 3100, arrivalRadius: 60) == .navigateOnly`. (b) NO FIX: `watchAdmission(distanceMeters: nil, arrivalRadius: 60) == .navigateOnly` — an unknown location must not be treated as arrival. (c) ARRIVED (vacuity): `watchAdmission(distanceMeters: 25, arrivalRadius: 60) == .startRitual`. (d) BEHAVIOURAL, driving the real object: build a `ReactionSession`, apply the `.navigateOnly` verdict's effect (open the camera only) and assert `session.phase == .idle && session.drop == nil`; then apply the `.startRitual` verdict's effect and assert `session.phase == .watching && session.drop?.id == drop.id`.
testCases.failsWhen: Legs (a), (b) and (d)'s first half FAIL against today's code: HomeScreen.swift:151 calls `reactionSession.startWatching(drop)` unconditionally, so no admission seam exists and the session enters `.watching` at 3.1 km. Vacuity is pinned by legs (c) and (d)'s second half — a fix that simply deletes `startWatching` from the card (reopening round-1 FLOW-10, which made the react→memory loop link-only) fails them, so the test cannot be satisfied by removing the feature.

testCases.name: testGroundSnapDeclineDoesNotEvictALiveDataLossMessage
testCases.asserts: Requires making the call site's criticality observable: hoist the string+flag into `static let groundSnapDeclineAdvisory = (message: "Couldn't find the ground here — move closer and try again", critical: false)` and have GeoARSessionManager.swift:2037 call `showPersistError(Self.groundSnapDeclineAdvisory.message, critical: Self.groundSnapDeclineAdvisory.critical)`. Then, on a @MainActor GeoARSessionManager (showPersistError needs no ARView), four legs. (a) EVICTION LEG: `showPersistError("Couldn't save the change — it may revert")`; then `showPersistError(Self.groundSnapDeclineAdvisory.message, critical: Self.groundSnapDeclineAdvisory.critical)`; assert `manager.persistErrorText == "Couldn't save the change — it may revert"`. (b) FLAG LEG: `XCTAssertFalse(GeoARSessionManager.groundSnapDeclineAdvisory.critical)`. (c) VISIBILITY VACUITY: with `persistErrorText == nil`, fire the decline advisory and assert `persistErrorText == groundSnapDeclineAdvisory.message` — the decline must still be seen when nothing outranks it. (d) DISCIPLINE VACUITY: `showPersistError("Couldn't save the change — it may revert")` then `showPersistError("Couldn't save the drop", critical: true)` and assert the second text wins — one genuine data-loss message must still be able to replace another.
testCases.failsWhen: Legs (a) and (b) FAIL against today's code: line 2037 omits the argument, so the decline is `critical: true` and overwrites the save-failure text at the assert in (a); the advisory constant does not exist, so (b) does not compile until the seam lands. Vacuity is pinned by (c) and (d) — (c) fails if the fix 'closes' the issue by suppressing the decline entirely, which would reopen ARPCFG-6 (the whole point of round 2's change was that the failure be visible rather than silently locking eye height), and (d) fails if the fix over-corrects the slot rule into never replacing a visible message.

cleanAreas: Deep-link admission/promotion (RootView.swift:187-204, AppRouter.swift:52-68). All four lens cases traced clean — clear stage, camera up, receive sheet up, memory up. Because .fullScreenCover has no interactive dismissal, every route to destination==nil passes through a dismissal and therefore through the cover's onDismiss, so there is no structural path that strands a queued link. receiveDropID is already nil inside .sheet's onDismiss, making the `receiveUp:` argument correct at both promotion sites; the single-slot newest-wins policy is explicit and tested.

Reveal hand-off and revealedDrop lifetime (RootView.swift:19, :193-221; ReceiveScreen.swift:117-121). The hand-off is a clean two-phase transaction: onReveal stashes, dismiss() completes, onDismiss clears the stash FIRST then starts the session and presents. revealedDrop is written on exactly one path and cleared on that same path's only continuation; 'Later', 'Close' and swipe-dismiss all take the else branch with it already nil. The old dismiss()+present-across-two-modifiers shape is gone.

Onboarding full run and the router-held beat (AppRouter.swift:44, :107-135; OnboardingView.swift:17, :66, :153-172). promise→demo→back→name→finish traced end to end with the beat surviving the cover swap; no view-local @State remains that a teardown can reset (draftName is re-seeded from @AppStorage on appear at OnboardingView.swift:127). Skip is correctly absent at beat 2 but the beat is still escapable because the 'Start dropping' CTA calls finish() unconditionally. The demo's clearRoomDrops() cannot destroy user content — the camera is unreachable before onboarding completes.

Camera exit under every condition (ARScreen.swift:186-207; ARSessionHolder.swift:61-72; GeoARSessionManager.swift:442-447, :512-518). The escape chevron is a true ZStack sibling above all three render states including the unsupported-device and lost-configure branches. Exit during a drag terminates the gesture without committing (onDisappear → cameraDidDisappear → markCameraHidden → cancelLiveEdit); exit during a watch session ends the ritual (RootView.swift:176-181); exit during the demo returns to the story beat rather than escaping onboarding.

Memory loop closure (RootView.swift:42-58, :111-133, :165-181; MemoryScreen.swift:34-41, :92-100; CreateWizard.swift:91-93). memory→send-one-back→create→share→Sent traced clean: endSession() is explicit before beginCreate() rather than relying on a dismiss race; MemoryScreen's X routes through destinationBinding, which ends the session in one place; CreateWizard's dismiss() clears createPrefill on the same edge. No path leaves a watch session alive past the screen it lives on.

Per-drop state destruction (GeoARSessionManager.swift:604-611, :1512-1539, :862-865, :1894-1902). All three former ad-hoc destroy loops now funnel through removePerDropState, which covers the previously-missed editingDropID/revealedDrops/liveEditingDrops subsets, closes the stale-nearest window at removal time, and invalidates the engine anchor. The edit-target vanish guard is live code rather than the unreachable branch it was, and VPS ownership now requires holder presence.

Reaction watermark durability (ReactionService.swift:37-50, :171-201, :254-258). The UserDefaults-backed per-drop watermark correctly distinguishes 'initial snapshot as history' from 'reaction that landed while this device was torn down', excludes own-uid and hasPendingWrites rows before toasting, and records on both the primed and live branches. stop() deliberately preserves the durable map while clearing the in-memory primed set — the right split. research.shipVerdict: DO NOT SHIP THIS BUILD; DO NOT CLOSE WAVE D ON IT. One more short, surgical round is required — not a re-architecture. Two defects are disqualifying on their own: STATE-L1 silently persists an edit to the WRONG drop, to disk and to Firestore, through a gesture the panel's own copy invites (hold still and look), reopening a defect the file documents as fixed at :232-238; and ARPCFG-R2-1 leaves the charter's 'zero draw-over' bar violated on roughly half of all tab flips by destroying the LiDAR mesh 0–200 ms before the pause that made the destruction pointless. Both were introduced or left open by round 2's own fixes for round-1 findings, which is exactly what this audit exists to catch. Round 3 scope should be exactly six items, all small and all with pure-function seams already designed by the panel: STATE-L1 (gesture liveness + re-bind refusal), ARPCFG-R2-1 (true-edge stamp AND grace > pauseGrace + one tick — both, not either), ARPCFG-R2-2 (one plan function, or stamp intent in beginRevealWarmup), UX-3 (one word today, separate advisory channel properly), UX-1 (guard the cancellation; move the timer to the single owner), RENDER-LENS-1 (idle 5 s + min-attach 10 s, extracted and table-tested). Land the accompanying tests in the same commit — every one of these six slipped past 140 green tests because the pure predicates are tested with their time-quantized inputs supplied as LITERALS (WaveDTests.swift:179-188 hands `cameraRecentlyVisible: true` directly), so the tests must drive the CALLER's clock, not the predicate's argument. The remaining six items do not gate the build: merge ARPCFG-R2-3/STATE-L4 and fix at least the capability term plus the false sharing comment at :1293-1296; carry UX-2 (with a fix that covers BOTH entrances), STATE-L2, STATE-L3, RENDER-LENS-2 and STATE-L5 into the Wave E backlog — but correct every comment that asserts an invariant the code does not hold (:444-447, :1293-1296, PersonSentinel :49-51) in the round-3 commit, because a false invariant comment is precisely how a closed finding gets re-litigated two rounds later.
research.waveExitAssessment:
WAVE D DOES NOT CLOSE ON THIS BUILD, and it cannot close on code review alone regardless of round 3 — but the gap is small and precisely nameable.

WHAT BLOCKS CLOSURE, CODE-SIDE (must be in the build the field tasks measure): (1) STATE-L1 — a wrong-drop persist to disk and Firestore, reachable from the designed slider interaction, introduced by round 2's STATE-1/FLOW-5 fix. Data integrity is not a wave-exit tradeable. (2) ARPCFG-R2-1 — the charter names four bars and 'zero draw-over' is one of them; ARPCFG-4 was the fix written for this exact scenario and it closes only for phi ≤ 0.2 (less, with tick drift). A charter bar that is still violated by the fix built for it is the definition of an open wave item. I would also require (3) UX-3 and (4) UX-1 in the same round purely because they are a one-word and a five-line fix respectively and both are regressions of invariants the counsel already made law — carrying them costs more in re-review than fixing them costs to write. RENDER-LENS-1 and ARPCFG-R2-2 should ride along; they are two-line and one-argument changes against the thermal and TTFO bars.

WHAT DOES NOT BLOCK CLOSURE: ARPCFG-R2-3/STATE-L4, UX-2, STATE-L2, STATE-L3, RENDER-LENS-2, STATE-L5. Each is a partial closure or hygiene item with bounded harm and none is a round-2 regression (I refuted the regression framing on STATE-L2, STATE-L3 and UX-2 specifically). They belong in the Wave E backlog with their comments corrected.

THE STRUCTURAL BLOCKER THE PANEL DID NOT NAME, which the supervisor should weigh most: NONE of Wave D's four bars has been MEASURED. Crash-free 99.5 %, ≥30 fps, not thermal .serious at 10 min, and zero draw-over are empirical claims, and every instrument that would substantiate them is on the deferred list — the on-device TSan run (RENDER-1 step 2), FT-28/FT-31, and RENDER-1 step 3's install-once decision which explicitly awaits that measurement. The one new instrument round 2 DID add, PersonSentinel's hold log, is defective in exactly the failure mode it exists to detect (RENDER-LENS-2) and latches after one line, so it will read clean under the sawtooth. That is the honest exit condition: Wave D closes when (a) round 3 lands the six surgical fixes with caller-clock tests, and (b) the named field tasks RUN and return numbers against the four bars on that build — not when the code review goes quiet. If the field tasks are genuinely deferred past wave close, then what closes is 'Wave D code review', and the four numeric bars remain formally unmet and must be carried as an explicit, named debt rather than assumed satisfied by a clean verdict. Fix RENDER-LENS-2's measurement before FT-28/FT-31 run, or the frame-budget investigation will be pointed at thermal throttling by an instrument the charter itself warns 'reads as thermal throttling but isn't'.

Positive note for the record, because it is load-bearing for the closure decision: the four genuinely hard round-1 blockers ARE closed and I verified them rather than assuming — RENDER-2's historyValid uniform (layout parity recomputed offset-by-offset, ping-pong pairing sound, invalid seed provably biases toward MORE occlusion so it cannot introduce draw-over), RENDER-3/4/7 (bailOut on all three encode exits, prepare() building outside the lock with a correct lost-race discard, lock order honoured in practice at :289/:314 vs :410-411), RENDER-5 (SourceBox empties at MidFieldDepthEstimator.swift:163 strictly before the handler at :173, and nothing else retains the ARKit originals), and the STATE-3/4/5/8-relevance destroy-path consolidation. The remaining defects are all in the same narrow seam — time-quantized couplings between a clock, a timer and a predicate that were never derived from one source of truth. That is one round's work, not a wave's.
